name: WATER III
question: In men with symptomatic 80–180 mL prostates, is Aquablation noninferior to transurethral laser enucleation for three-month symptom improvement and procedural safety?

design.population: 202 men with moderate to severe lower urinary tract symptoms and prostate volumes of 80–180 mL were enrolled; 186 underwent surgery.
design.description: International, multicenter, partially randomized, nonblinded noninferiority trial
design.locator: PubMed abstract, Methods and Key Findings; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04801381, Study Design

verdictNote: Three-month IPSS noninferiority shown; the abstract omits the safety decision threshold.
takeaway: Partially randomized WATER III compared Aquablation with transurethral laser enucleation for 80–180 mL prostates. Three-month IPSS improvement met Bayesian noninferiority, while retrograde ejaculation and persistent stress incontinence were reported less often after Aquablation.

reports.label: Three-month primary report
reports.citation: Ritter M, Stein J, Barber N, et al. "WATER III: A Prospective, Partially Randomized Trial of Aquablation Therapy Versus Transurethral Laser Enucleation of the Prostate for Treatment of Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms." *Eur Urol Focus.* 2026;12(2):266-274. doi:10.1016/j.euf.2026.01.006
reports.followUp: 3 months for the coprimary efficacy and safety endpoints

results.measure: Mean IPSS change from baseline to 3 months; Bayesian estimated difference in change (Aquablation minus laser enucleation), points
results.note: 95% credible interval; posterior probability of noninferiority >0.999. Arm-specific analyzed denominators are absent from the abstract.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Key Findings and Limitations

results.measure: Clavien–Dindo grade ≥2 or grade 1 complications persisting at 3 months; Bayesian risk difference, percentage points
results.note: 95% credible interval; posterior probability of noninferiority 0.952. The abstract does not give the prespecified decision threshold or event denominators. Estimated difference is model-based, not subtraction of the displayed rates.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Methods and Key Findings and Limitations

harms.label: Retrograde ejaculation at 3 months
harms.locator: PubMed abstract, Key Findings and Limitations
harms.note: P <0.001; event counts and denominators are absent from the abstract.

harms.label: Persistent stress urinary incontinence at 3 months
harms.locator: PubMed abstract, Key Findings and Limitations
harms.note: P <0.05; event counts and denominators are absent from the abstract.

delivery.label: Surgery and analysis cohorts
delivery.locator: PubMed abstract, Key Findings and Limitations
delivery.note: 186 of 202 enrolled men underwent surgery; 170 had 3-month data, including 66 randomized and 104 nonrandomized men. Arm-specific analysis counts are not stated.

delivery.label: Operative approaches
delivery.value: AquaBeam waterjet ablation with bladder-neck electroresection for residual tissue and hemostasis versus center-standard holmium or thulium laser enucleation.
delivery.note: Registry protocol description; operative details are not in the PubMed abstract.

results.note: The meeting abstract does not give a between-arm effect estimate or randomized-only analysis.
